'''Heavy Caliber''' is a [[Corrupted Mod]] that increases damage of [[Primary Weapon]]s (excluding [[Shotgun]]s) at the cost of increased [[spread]] (reducing accuracy). Some weapons will have additional spread added, in addition to the base amount.

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*Instead of reducing the accuracy by 5% per rank, each rank increases spread by a specific value per rank depending on the weapon.
*Damage bonus stacks additively with similar mods, such as {{M|Serration}}.
**Since the two stack additively and Heavy Caliber costs 2 more mod capacity for the same bonus, combining the two is slightly less efficient in terms of damage per capacity cost. Maxed Serration grants +11.79% bonus damage per 1 mod capacity, while maxed Heavy Caliber grants +10.31% bonus damage per mod capacity. Combining the two, Serration and Heavy Caliber grant +11% bonus damage per 1 mod capacity, which is +0.79% less bonus damage per capacity than Serration alone.
*Added spread is not affected by bonuses that increase accuracy, such as {{M|Twitch}} or {{M|Guided Ordnance}}.
**For example, a {{Weapon|Braton}} with {{M|Heavy Caliber}} and {{M|Twitch}} will have a max deviation of {{Math|{{Tooltip|5.0|Braton's Max Deviation}} {{mul}} (1 - {{M|Twitch|40%}}) + {{M|Heavy Caliber|2.97}}|t=y|bf=y|round=0.1}} degrees.
*Causes beam of all continuous weapons to noticeably wobble.

==Trivia==
*When it was first released, Heavy Caliber's original penalty was an increase in ''recoil'' as well as damage. However the recoil penalty did not affect recoil-less weapons ({{Weapon|Flux Rifle}}, {{Weapon|Ignis}}, {{Weapon|Synapse}}, [[:Category:Bow|bows]] and {{Weapon|Lanka}} among others), effectively acting as another instance of {{M|Serration}}. This was confirmed to be unintentional in [http://www.twitch.tv/warframe/b/469098182 Warframe Prime Time - Episode 2 (9:40)]. The mod's penalty was changed in {{ver|10.4}}.

{{Codex|Spike enemies to the wall or reel them in with this automatic harpoon gun.}}
The '''Harpak''' is a {{Faction|Grineer}} harpoon gun standard issue for [[Drekar Elite Lancer]]s. It has two firing modes; its primary firing mode fires a burst of three harpoon projectiles, while its [[Alternate Fire]] fires a chain-tethered harpoon that will damage foes and pull most targets towards the user.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Primary fire shoots three harpoons in a burst.
**Bolts fired stick to their target, and will fling bodies on kill.
**The body will damage targets in its path.
**Flung bodies help in dealing with crowds.
**Corpses can be pinned to terrain.
*[[Alternate Fire]] shoots a harpoon that inflicts a guaranteed {{D|Puncture}} proc and can reel enemies in close and knock them down.
**Can 'pull' humanoid flyers (such as [[Hellion]]s) down, and pull enemies that are stunned by Warframe powers.
**The harpoon pull can interrupt enemy casting/power animations, including the charge-up for {{E|Railgun MOA}}s.
**[[Knockdown]] leaves target open for melee [[finisher]]s.
*Can use the Harpak-exclusive {{M|Exposing Harpoon}} mod.

{{Advantages|name=Harpak|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|}}

{{Disadvantages|name=Harpak|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
*Projectiles have travel time with arcing.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Harpak's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}
This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}.

==Notes==
*Enemies can be pulled into bottomless pits or inaccessible areas, killing them instantly.
*The Harpak's secondary fire mode (default {{Keybind|Mouse 3}}) fires a tethered harpoon that can pull enemies towards the player and causes a guaranteed {{D|Puncture}} proc. The harpoon costs 1 ammo to fire.
**The secondary fire mode has a maximum range of '''50''' meters, projectile flight speed modifiers ([[Riven Mods]]) and mods like {{M|Terminal Velocity}} will increase this range. While the harpoon will still hit enemies up to its maximum range, it will only pull them if they are at a distance smaller or equal to '''40 '''meters, projectile flight speed modifiers ([[Riven Mods]]) or {{M|Terminal Velocity}} do '''not '''increase this range.
**It seems that the harpoon is unable to break Resource Deposits (yet it works just fine on explosive barrels and Storage Containers, more testing required)
*Enemies killed via the secondary fire, are pulled a significant distance with momentum. This momentum allows the Harpak to kill an enemy behind the first target by sheer force.
*The Harpak's firing noise increases in pitch as the magazine depletes.
*Mechanically, the Harpak is nearly identical to the previously introduced {{Weapon|Paracyst}}, as both rifles are burst-fire projectile weapons that shoot out pulling harpoons as their secondary fire mode.

==Trivia==
*The Harpak's name is derived from ''[[wikipedia:Harpoon|Harpoon]]'', a long spear-like instrument used in fishing, whaling, sealing, and other marine hunting.
**It might also be influenced by the ''[[wikipedia:Harpax|Harpax]]'', a Roman naval siege device invented by Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa which was intended to launch harpoons into naval vessels and reel them in for boarding, similar to the Harpak's alternate fire.
*The Harpak was first presented in the [https://warframe.com/echoes/? Update 17 Teaser Site], but its name was not revealed until the release of the [https://www.youtube.com/watch?t=32&v=oAVA_vGb9_w Echoes of the Sentients Highlight Video.]
*The word in [[Grineer Language|Grineer]] found by the barrel of the weapon, {{GrineerScript|Grineer}}, spells out ''Grineer''.
*Oddly, the Harpak's alternate fire can be seen ricocheting from enemies when they are already under the effects of crowd control such as an {{D|Impact}} [[Proc]] and will harmlessly float in the air away from the target for a few seconds.

==Known Bugs ==
*Unlike previous projectile weapons, the Harpak's bolts will not share the same color as the ones selected for both its primary and secondary attack.
*In the ballroom simulacrum room, using the Harpak on an enemy close to the statues will result in their body turning ragdoll and suddenly dying should they touch either of them.
*{{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from harpoon.

{{Codex|A bloodsucker. This symbiotic burst-rifle leeches health to forge its ammo and then restores health with each headshot.}}<section begin="intro" />The '''Hema''' is an {{Faction|Infested}} burst-fire rifle that uses no ammunition, instead demanding a [[health]] sacrifice to reload. It fires three-round bursts of {{D|Viral}} agents, life stealing on [[Enemy Body Parts|headshots]] to heal the user.<section end="intro" />

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals {{D|Viral}} damage.
*This weapon does not use ammo pickups; health is converted to ammo.
**Scales with the amount of ammo restored, up to '''5%''' of the user's max health.
*[[Enemy Body Parts|Headshots]] have '''5%''' [[Life Steal]].
*Can use the Hema-exclusive {{M|Necrophagic Vigor}}.
*Innate {{Pol|Madurai}} polarity.

{{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
* Lifesteal of headshot provides a method of healing.
* Functionally infinite ammo.
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
* Health drain can be detrimental in some cases.
* Projectiles have travel time and low flight speed.
}}
{{WeaponComparison|Coda Hema}}

==Acquisition ==
The Hema's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Bio Lab|Bio Lab]] in the [[dojo]].
{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

== Notes ==
*The Hema is a highly accurate rifle that heals the player on headshots. To reload however, the player must lay out their arm as the weapon sucks some of their health. It will drain up to 5% of the player's max health depending on how much ammo needs to be replenished to the magazine. With the unmodded magazine size of 60, each bullet reloaded drains '''0.083%''' max health.
**If the player is at 3 or lower health, it will not reload and the player will have no ammo until they get more health.
*Increasing magazine size does not increase the health drain per magazine. Thus, it decreases the drain per bullet.
* It can be considered a more effective anti-Grineer and Corpus version of the {{Weapon|Paracyst}}, as its base {{D|Viral}} damage allows for {{D|Corrosive}} and {{D|Heat}} for Grineer, or {{D|Toxin}} and {{D|Magnetic}} for Corpus.

== Known Bugs ==

* {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits.

== Tips==

*Like all burst fire weapons in Warframe, you must time your clicks in order to fire the weapon at its maximum speed. Mashing the fire button will only stall and fire the weapon at different rates. Frame rates below ~30 FPS will also begin to slow the weapon down.
*The weapon doesn't require ammo pickups, meaning there is no risk of running out of ammo in endless missions provided the player still has health.
*Using {{WF|Inaros}} or {{WF|Nidus}} is highly suggested due to their high base health, their various means of self-healing, and the latter's innate health regeneration. {{WF|Wisp}} is another good option, due to the significant health and constant healing granted by her {{A|Reservoirs}}' Vitality Motes.

==Trivia ==
*The Hema is the first weapon in Warframe that drains the player's health in order to reload.
*''Hema'' is a word derived from the Greek word ''haima'' (αἷμα), meaning 'blood', and is used as a prefix to refer to objects or conditions relating to blood, e.g. "Hematology", "Hematoxin", etc.
*Prior to {{ver|32.2}}, the health drained by the Hema on reloading contributed to {{WF|Chroma}}'s Fury buff from {{A|Vex Armor}}, albeit in very small amounts.
* This is the second non-[[Archwing]] weapon in the game to have infinite/rechargeable ammunition after the {{Weapon|Cycron}} and the first primary weapon with such a feature, with the {{Weapon|Fulmin}}, {{Weapon|Flux Rifle}}, {{Weapon|Shedu}}, {{Weapon|Basmu}}, and {{Weapon|Haalvu}} following this trend.

'''Hemorrhage''' is a pistol [[mod]] that gives a chance of every {{D|Impact}} status effect to produce an instance of a {{D|Slash}} proc. This chance is doubled when the weapon's [[fire rate]] is below 2.5.

==Notes==
* Cannot produce multiple procs in a single instance of damage alongside any other {{D|Slash}} sources such as a weapon's innate {{D|Slash}} or the debuff from {{A|Seeking Talons}}.
* This mod can proc a maximum of one time per projectile, and its effectiveness is increased with Multishot.
** Inflicting multiple stacks of {{D|Impact}} in single instance of damage does not allow this mod to proc more than once, nor will it increase the chance of the mod proccing.
*{{M|Hard Engage}} works with this mod.
*[[Fire Rate]] buffs such as {{WF|Gauss}}' {{A|Redline}}, [[Wisp|Wisp's]] Haste [[Reservoirs]], and  {{Arcane|Arcane Velocity}} can negatively impact this mod's performance since it may increase the weapon's fire rate past 2.5.
* If the weapon's fire rate is exactly 2.5, it will '''not''' receive the 2x bonus.

'''Higasa''' is {{WF|Koumei}}'s [[Signature Weapon|signature]] gun umbrella. Its primary fire shoots burst-fire rounds and that builds charges on kills to allow use of the [[Alternate Fire]] involving a powerful {{D|Blast}} laser. [[Zoom|Aiming]] down sights opens the umbrella to project a field that nullifies projectiles and charges the Alternate Fire.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage on its primary fire and pure {{D|Blast}} damage on its [[Alternate Fire]].
*[[Zoom|Aiming]] projects a field that blocks frontal projectiles.
**The field closes when [[Reload]]ing or charging the Alternate Fire.
*Primary fire shoots 5-round bursts.
*Alternate Fire charges a powerful laser.
**Cannot fire without a full gauge.
***Using Alternate Fire without a full gauge still drains it completely.
**Killing an enemy with the primary fire will fill '''10%''' of the gauge. Blocking an enemy attack fills '''10%''' of the gauge per second for '''2''' seconds.
***Blocking another enemy attack while gauge is filling from blocking an enemy attack will refresh the duration.
**Innate 2 meters [[Punch Through]].
*Can use the Higasa-exclusive {{M|Higasa Serration}} mod.

{{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Burst|

}}

==Acquisition==
Higasa's blueprint and components can be obtained from [[Shrine Defense]] on [[Saya's Visions]], [[Earth]]. Access requires completion of [[Saya's Vigil]] and [[Once Awake]].

Alternatively they can be purchased from [[Koumei's Shrine]] in [[Cetus]] with {{Resource|Fate Pearl}}, which are dropped by the [[Infested Oni]] at the end of Shrine Defense in quantities of 14-18 (20-24 on [[The Steel Path]]). Each component blueprint require 45 and the main blueprint requires 135, totaling 270 Fate Pearls for the whole set.

==Crafting==
Higasa also requires {{Resource|Fate Pearl}} to craft; 14 per component and 5 for the main blueprint, to a total of 47 Fate Pearls.
